transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is I just don’t feel like myself anymore. It’s like I’ve gotten… quieter, flatter, I don’t know how else to put it. I barely talk to people now, even people I see all the time. I used to at least make small talk, you know, say a few things, joke a little maybe, but lately I just kind of stand there or keep my head down.

And at work, doing the cleaning route, even starting it feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. Not just physically, but like I can’t get myself moving. I’ll look at what needs to be done and it feels like there’s this heavy wall between me and doing it. I still try, but everything takes more out of me than it should. I’m just… flat and quiet, and it’s not how I remember being.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah… I have. I mean, it’s not always like I’m crying or anything obvious like that, but it’s there most of the time, kind of sitting in the background. Since the move, especially, I’ve felt this sadness and heaviness that just doesn’t really leave.

Some days other things take up more space in my head, but even then, underneath it, I still feel low. Like the energy is gone, and things I used to care about don’t pull me in the same way. And I feel guilty too, like I should be doing better or handling things better, but I’m just not. It’s been pretty constant, more days than not… honestly, most of the time.
Do you hear voices when no one is there?

Yeah… I do. I wasn’t sure if I should say that right away, because it sounds strange when I say it out loud, but yes.

It happens mostly when I’m mopping after hours, when the building is quiet and everybody’s gone or mostly gone. I’ll be going down the hallway, or near the stairwell, and I’ll hear a man’s voice. Clear. Not like a thought in my head exactly, and not like remembering somebody talking. It sounds like he’s right there, like standing off by the stairs.

Sometimes he just says my name. Other times it’ll be something like, “You missed a spot,” like he’s watching what I’m doing. And I’ll stop and look over, because it feels real enough that I expect to see somebody there, but there’s nobody. No one in the stairwell, no one behind me. It leaves me feeling kind of rattled, because I can’t explain it away easily.
Have you ever heard the voice during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… yes, I think so. That’s part of what scares me, because it wasn’t only when I was at my lowest.

There was a stretch, maybe several weeks, where my mood had lifted a little. Not like I was back to normal, but I was eating more regularly and getting through work a bit better. I could do my route without feeling completely crushed by it every minute, and meals didn’t feel like such a chore.

But even then, I’d still hear my name in the stairwell. Just my name, clear enough that I’d stop what I was doing and look around. And during that same time I was still pretty convinced the hallway cameras were being used to track me, like someone was watching where I went in the building. So… yeah, even when I wasn’t feeling as depressed, that part didn’t really go away.
Was there ever a time when the voice or the feeling that the cameras were tracking you lasted for at least two weeks when you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’m careful saying “not depressed at all,” because I don’t know if I ever felt completely fine, like nothing was wrong. But there was definitely a stretch of several weeks where the depression had lifted some.

I was eating more normally, or at least meals didn’t feel like such a fight. I was getting through my shifts a little better, doing the mopping and the cleaning without that same heavy feeling pressing down every second. I wasn’t exactly happy, but I wasn’t in that deep low place the way I had been.

And during that time, the voice still happened. I’d still hear my name in the stairwell, clear enough that I’d stop and look, like someone had called me. And the camera thing was still there too. I still felt pretty convinced the hallway cameras were tracking where I went, like somebody was keeping tabs on me through them.

So… yes, there was a period of at least a couple weeks, probably several, when my mood was better, but those things didn’t really stop.
During this time, did you ever lose interest in almost everything you usually care about?

Yeah… I did. That’s actually one of the things I noticed most, because I used to have little things that kind of kept me going, even if they weren’t big things.

Like, I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays. I’d get my stuff ready the night before sometimes, check the line, pack a thermos, all that. Even if I didn’t catch much, just being out there mattered to me. But lately, or during that time, I’d just let the gear sit. I’d think about going and then it was like… what’s the point, you know? It didn’t feel like it would give me anything back.

Same with crosswords in the morning. I used to sit with coffee and do them, kind of wake my brain up that way. Now I’ll look at the paper and just leave it there. And at work, I used to like showing the younger guys little tricks, like how to strip a floor clean without making a mess of it, stuff I’ve learned over the years. I used to take some pride in that. But I don’t really get that feeling anymore. Mostly I just do what I have to do and let the rest sit.
Do you feel hopeless?

Yeah… I do. Maybe not every single second in the same way, but it comes over me a lot.

It’s like I keep looking at my life and thinking I should’ve done better. I lost my old place, and I can’t stop turning that over in my head like it proves something about me, like I failed at being a grown man, failed everybody who ever counted on me. I know people have setbacks, I know that in my head, but it doesn’t feel that way when I’m alone with it. It feels like I let my whole life slip out of my hands.

And then it spreads to things that probably don’t even make sense. Like if the church pantry is short on supplies, I’ll find myself thinking, well, I should’ve noticed sooner, I should’ve helped more, somehow that’s on me. Or if a hallway at work gets missed or isn’t as clean as it should be, I take it like it means I’m useless, like I can’t even keep up with the basic things I’m supposed to do.

So, yeah… hopeless, and guilty too, I guess. Like no matter what I do, I’m already behind and I’m not going to catch up.
During that time when your mood had lifted, were you still feeling down nearly every day?

Not nearly every day in that same heavy way, no. That’s why it stands out to me, I guess.

There was a stretch of several weeks where my mood had lifted some. I don’t want to make it sound like I was suddenly cheerful or back to normal, because I wasn’t exactly that. But I was getting through meals better, and work was a little easier to push through. I could do the cleaning, get through the shifts, without feeling crushed every minute.

But even with that, the other stuff was still there. I still heard my name in the stairwell sometimes, clear enough that I’d stop and check. And I still felt like the hallway cameras were being used to track me, like somebody was watching where I went.

So if you mean was I still down nearly every day during that better stretch… I’d say no, not like before. My mood was better for a while, but those experiences didn’t stop.
Was there ever a time when you were not feeling depressed at all, but you were still hearing the voice or believing the cameras were tracking you?

Yeah… yes, there was. I mean, I don’t know if I’d say I felt perfectly fine, because I don’t think I’ve felt “perfectly fine” in a long time, but there was a stretch of several weeks where I wasn’t feeling depressed the way I had been.

Like I was eating a little better, not having to force every bite as much, and work was… not easy exactly, but I could get through it. I could show up, do the halls, take care of the trash, the floors, the regular stuff, and it didn’t feel like I was carrying a cinder block on my chest the whole time.

But even then, the voice stuff didn’t go away. I’d still hear my name in the stairwell sometimes, clear enough that I’d stop and look around, like somebody had just called me. And the cameras in the hallway… I still believed they were tracking me. It wasn’t like, “Oh, that was just because I was depressed.” Even when my mood had lifted some, I still felt watched by them.

So, yeah. The depression had backed off for a while, but those things were still happening.
Have there been at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or felt the cameras were tracking you, and you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yes… yes, I think so. More than two weeks, actually. It was several weeks where the depression had lifted some. I don’t mean I was suddenly happy or anything like that, but I wasn’t down in that same constant way.

I was eating a little better, getting through meals without having to force everything, and work was a little more manageable. I could go in and do the cleaning, get through the hallways and the regular jobs, and it wasn’t crushing me every minute like before.

But during that same stretch, I still heard my name in the stairwell. I’d stop because it sounded real enough, like somebody had just called me. And I still believed the hallway cameras were being used to track where I was going. That didn’t really let up just because my mood was better. So… yes, there was at least a couple weeks like that.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t think.

I’ve had times where I maybe got through the day better, or I felt a little lighter compared to how bad it had been, but I wouldn’t call it unusually high or euphoric. I don’t remember feeling like I had all this extra energy or like I was on top of the world or anything.

Mostly, if my mood lifted, it was more like… I could function a bit more. Like I could do what I needed to do without dragging myself through every single step. But not this big burst of energy or feeling overly happy. If anything, I’d probably notice that because it would be pretty different for me. So, no, I don’t think I’ve had a period like that.
Was there ever a period of at least one month when you were hearing the voice or believed the cameras were tracking you?

Yes… definitely more than a month. It’s been going on for, I’d say, about eleven months now.

Not every single minute of every day in the exact same way, but the voice and the feeling about the cameras watching or tracking me… that’s been there for most of this past year. I keep thinking back and trying to place when it started, and it’s hard because at first I sort of brushed it off, like maybe I was tired or maybe I misunderstood something. But it didn’t just stop.

So yes, if you’re asking whether it lasted at least a month, then yes. It’s been closer to eleven months.

Mostly, if my mood lifted, it was more like… I could function a bit more. Like I could do what I needed to do without dragging myself through every single step. But not this big burst of energy or feeling overly happy. If anything, I’d probably notice that because it would be pretty different for me. So, no, I don’t think I’ve had a period like that.

I keep thinking back and trying to place when it started, and it’s hard because at first I sort of brushed it off, like maybe I was tired or maybe I misunderstood something. But it didn’t just stop.

So yes, if you’re asking whether it lasted at least a month, then yes. It’s been closer to eleven months.
